pr_title: Fixed source generator endpoint delegate handling for nullable scenarios
pr_body:
Fixed source generator endpoint delegate handling for nullable scenarios by storing the `WrappedResponseType` and using it to check for nullability.

Fixes #54172

issue_context.title: Request delegate generator produces CS8073 for ValueTask<T?> results

Oh man, my bad, I thought that @captainsafia was asking for anyone, I misread her question. Thanks tho.

I've understood where the problem is and why it occurs. It seems there's a bug in the response type check itself, where when the response type is annotated as nullable, the code ends up checking if the Task is null, as seen here:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c7c76d7d3bb30e29e8386d1a3e6dae9e307fd0de/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/StaticRouteHandlerModel/StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L91-L97

And here:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c7c76d7d3bb30e29e8386d1a3e6dae9e307fd0de/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/StaticRouteHandlerModel/StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L383-L389

The problem is that the IF check is incorrect. When it checks: `endpoint.Response?.ResponseType?.NullableAnnotation`, what it actually checks is whether the inner type of the `awaitable type` is nullable or not. If the type were, for instance, `Task<bool>?`, it would never fall into this check because `bool` was not annotated as `nullable`.

With that said, I believe the correct procedure would be to check from the awaitable type itself; however, to do this, I would have to modify how the [EndpointResponse](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/StaticRouteHandlerModel/EndpointResponse.cs) class works.

So that this line:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/c7c76d7d3bb30e29e8386d1a3e6dae9e307fd0de/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/StaticRouteHandlerModel/EndpointResponse.cs#L30

Stores the type itself, and not the string.

I would like to hear your opinions on this @captainsafia and @gfoidl, and if everything is okay, I plan to open the PR.

Yep, the type itself should be stored, so that it can be checked whether it's a valuetype or a referencetype later on.
